To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the formation of crosslinks in the viral capsid drives its structural transformation from a semimature to a more mature conformation, which is a prerequisite for packaging the viral chromosome.
crosslinks drive conformational switching during HK97 capsid maturation by promoting the capture of surface loops that are otherwise mobile.

the conformational transition from EI-I/II to Balloon is accompanied by a switch in the crosslinking pattern, that crosslinking promotes the transition to balloon, and that the conformation of EI-I/IL favors crosslinking.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structural basis of capsid expansion in tailed bacteriophage HK97.
how a viral capsid can be converted into a new form, and how the structural transformation can be driven by crosslink formation.
how a viral capsid can expand to accommodate the genome.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the crosslinking of the mobile surface loops in the HK97 capsids promotes the structural transformation from EI-I/II to Balloon, and this structural transition is essential for the maturation of the HK97 capsid.
the capsid expansion of HK97 capsid is driven by the crosslinking of mobile loops on the capsid surface, and the conformational switching between EI-I/II and Balloon states is a switch-like process.

the crosslinking that is induced by the binding of the scaffold protein to the procapsid shell promotes the structural transition of the capsid from an EI-I/II to a more expanded balloon-like structure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
crosslink formation promotes a conformational switch that drives capsid expansion.
the formation of intersubunit crosslinks in the procapsid drives capsid expansion by promoting the capture of a mobile loop in the major capsid protein.
the crosslinking of the mobile surface loops of HK97 capsid drives capsid expansion.
The main takeaway from our work is that
crosslinking of mobile surface loops can drive capsid expansion, and that this process is coupled to the maturation of the HK97 capsid.
the crosslinking of surface loops that are mobile during maturation promotes the transition from a semimature to a mature state by shifting the equilibrium between two conformers.
the crosslinked state is more stable and that the crosslinking process is coupled to capsid expansion, a finding that may be relevant to many other capsid systems.
